why_ai: A commissioned notary must personally witness the signer, at a table or over video, and carries the liability, but the act is a commodity and remote notarization with automated identity proofing is eroding the in-person share.
why_clarity: A valid act and a clean package are exactly defined by statute and lender checklists and recur thousands of times, though identity mistakes surface only months later.
why_digital: Starts from a person and a plastic ID at a kitchen table and ends in a wet-ink package couriered back, with orders arriving through online marketplaces.

why_ai: Someone commissioned must attend each signing, though the hands-on part is a short appointment, title companies treat agents as interchangeable, and hybrid and remote closings chip away at volume.
why_clarity: Lender checklists define a correct package and funding reveals errors within days, while identity failures on seller signings show up much later.
why_digital: Documents and orders move online, but the work is a physical appointment and a paper package shipped back.

why_ai: The borrower is already verified, so the job is a short routine appointment that hybrid closings and package-checking software steadily shrink.
why_clarity: Every package has an exact checklist, near-identical signings recur at volume, and scanbacks or funding expose errors within hours.
why_digital: Package PDFs arrive digitally, but signing is wet ink at the borrower's table and the originals go by courier.

why_ai: Facing a possible impostor is adversarial, high-stakes judgement under personal liability, made at a brief appointment, and rising deepfake fraud pushes title companies toward trusted in-person notaries.
why_clarity: The procedure is codified, but whether the signer was really the owner is often learned only months later from a claim.
why_digital: The decisive evidence is a person and a physical credential examined face to face, with title companies routing work to approved local panels.

why_ai: A notary and witnesses must be present, often at homes and bedsides, to observe a frail signer's awareness and free will, and contested estates make that human record more valuable, though some states now allow remote acts.
why_clarity: Witness and certificate rules are codified, but whether the ceremony holds up is decided in probate years later.
why_digital: Ceremonies happen at homes, offices and bedsides on paper, booked locally by attorneys and families.

why_ai: Statute makes the notary keep the journal personally, but completing and retrieving entries is record-keeping software can do.
why_clarity: Each state lists the required fields exactly, though an entry's adequacy is tested only when an act is challenged.
why_digital: Entries are captured by hand with signatures and thumbprints at the table, increasingly in apps, and retrieved on request.

why_ai: Facilitation is routing paper through government offices, a service that rule engines and online state portals can largely absorb.
why_clarity: Certification chains are fixed per document and destination, recur constantly, and offices accept or reject within days.
why_digital: Paper originals with wet seals are mailed or walked through offices, though customers order from facilitators anywhere in the country.

why_ai: Bedside and jail signings need a commissioned person on site judging identity without an ID and the signer's capacity, though the physical task itself is brief and some facilities allow video acts.
why_clarity: Identity alternatives are codified by state, but each facility and signer differs and challenges come years later.
why_digital: Entirely in-person in hospitals, care homes and jails, arranged locally by families and social workers.

why_ai: Signers want a commissioned notary who speaks their language and whom their community trusts, at a short in-person appointment that translation tools cannot carry.
why_clarity: The act is codified, but interpreter rules vary and misunderstandings surface only in later disputes.
why_digital: In-person acts booked through community word of mouth, with few remote options in other languages.

why_ai: State law still requires a commissioned notary on the call, but identity proofing, recording and journaling are software and notaries are interchangeable.
why_clarity: MISMO-style identity steps and state rules define each session, which repeats identically and passes or fails on the spot.
why_digital: Credentials are captured by camera and the whole act happens and is delivered online to signers anywhere.

why_ai: Assigning, confirming and tracking orders is coordination work that dispatch software and language-model agents can take over.
why_clarity: An order is filled on time and completed cleanly or not, across thousands of near-identical orders a month.
why_digital: Orders, assignments and status updates are digital, though the result is a physical appointment, and title companies buy from services nationwide.

why_ai: Screen-based fraud and threshold work, protected mainly by the adversarial race against remote impostors.
why_clarity: Sessions are reviewed against defined identity rules at volume, though confirmed fraud outcomes arrive late.
why_digital: Session recordings, credential images and device signals in, risk decisions out, all inside the platform.

why_ai: Summarising fifty states' notary statutes and answering hotline questions is content work language models increasingly do.
why_clarity: Statutes give the content a fixed basis, but guidance quality has no quick objective check.
why_digital: Statutes in, handbooks, courses and hotline answers out, with some in-person conferences and seminars.

why_ai: Ranking agents and suggesting fees from order data is product analytics that automates readily.
why_clarity: Orders fill or not and complete cleanly or not, with outcomes known within days across huge volume.
why_digital: Order and outcome data in, rankings and dashboards out, entirely online.

why_ai: The margin is coordination between title companies and agents, which dispatch software and marketplaces compress.
why_clarity: Each order has a defined clean outcome and recurs at volume, with errors known within a day.
why_digital: Orders and documents move online and clients buy nationally, but delivery is a physical signing by a contracted agent.

why_ai: Mass-issued bonds and small policies are underwritten almost automatically, with a regulated insurer still required to stand behind them.
why_clarity: Issuance is a fixed procedure repeated for every new commission, though claims emerge years after the act.
why_digital: Applications, issuance and claims run online, sold through associations and supply vendors.

why_ai: Statutory authority to commission and discipline notaries stays with the state, though commission processing itself automates.
why_clarity: Commissioning follows statute, but each complaint investigation differs and resolves slowly.
why_digital: Applications, exams and complaints are handled largely online within a fixed state jurisdiction.

why_ai: Recording is a statutory public function that will persist, though document examination is increasingly automated.
why_clarity: Recording requirements are codified and each document is accepted or rejected quickly, while fraud surfaces later.
why_digital: Instruments arrive mostly by eRecording and are examined on screen, but each office serves one county.

why_ai: Courts rely on a named, qualified examiner who inspects originals and testifies under cross-examination.
why_clarity: Methods are documented, but each case is different and the verdict comes from a court months later.
why_digital: Original documents and seals are examined physically, reports are written on screen, and experts are retained across regions.

why_ai: Course content built from public law and personal experience is directly substitutable by AI tutors and free material.
why_clarity: Curricula are defined and exams objective, though whether training produces good agents is rarely measured.
why_digital: Courses, videos and communities delivered and sold entirely online.

why_ai: Stamps and journals are commodity products, and e-journal apps are software that larger platforms can absorb.
why_clarity: Each order is a defined product made to the commission's specification, repeated for every notary.
why_digital: Orders and commission data arrive online, but seals and journals are manufactured and shipped as physical goods.
